script.text: Alright, let’s study Chapter 15: PMP Mindset / People & Process. This is one of those PMP areas where you want to understand both the terminology and the project manager mindset behind it.

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: Exactly. The PMP rarely rewards memorizing words only. It wants you to recognize the situation, identify what process or principle is being tested, and choose the next best action.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: One key point is this: Domain 1: People (14 Tasks)

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: And the way to think about that for the exam is to connect it to the project manager’s responsibility. Task 1: Manage Conflict

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: One key point is this: One of the most fundamental responsibilities of a project manager is managing conflicts between stakeholders on a project.

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: And the way to think about that for the exam is to connect it to the project manager’s responsibility. Conflicts can occur:

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: One key point is this: Between team members

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: And the way to think about that for the exam is to connect it to the project manager’s responsibility. Between sponsors and team members

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: One key point is this: Between suppliers and the project manager

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: And the way to think about that for the exam is to connect it to the project manager’s responsibility. Between any combination of stakeholders

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: One key point is this: For any conflict:

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: And the way to think about that for the exam is to connect it to the project manager’s responsibility. Understand the source and stage of the conflict

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: One key point is this: Why did the conflict happen?

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: And the way to think about that for the exam is to connect it to the project manager’s responsibility. What was the main underlying reason?

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: One key point is this: How did it escalate to this?

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: And the way to think about that for the exam is to connect it to the project manager’s responsibility. Analyze the context of the conflict

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: One key point is this: Evaluate/recommend/reconcile the appropriate conflict resolution solution

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: And the way to think about that for the exam is to connect it to the project manager’s responsibility. Example of conflict between two team members:

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: One key point is this: Interpret the main cause (source) of the conflict

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: And the way to think about that for the exam is to connect it to the project manager’s responsibility. Speak to the team members

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: So the big takeaway is not just knowing the definition. You want to ask: what is happening in the scenario, who is impacted, what process should be used, and what should the project manager do next?

script.speaker: Jordan
script.text: Right. Slow down, do not jump straight to escalation, and use the correct PMP process. That is how this chapter turns into points on the exam.
